headline: In mosaku, 模 is a daiyōji replacing 摸.
Tamari is the continuative stem of the verb 溜まる (tamaru, “to gather, to accumulate”).
Ōgon is from Middle Chinese 黃金 (MC hwang kim, “yellow + metal”).
ダウン is from English down.
Uwamawaru is the bound form 上 (uwa-) of 上 (ue, “up; top”) plus 回る (mawaru, “to go around; to prevail”).
フォーム covers “form” and “foam”, and the source takes both from English.
Sentō is from Middle Chinese 戰鬪, and the source compares Mandarin 戰鬥 (zhàndòu).
Kiza is short for 気障り (kizawari, “disagreeable”).
ビールス is a learned borrowing from Latin virus.
モニター is from English monitor.
Muimi is 無 (mu-, “without”) plus 意味 (imi, “meaning”).
Zeimusho is, by surface analysis, 税務 (zeimu) plus 署 (-sho).
Chō, “butterfly”, is from Middle Chinese 蝶 (MC thep|dep) and passed through tepu, tefu, tewu and teu.
Akaji is 赤 (aka, “red”) plus 字 (ji, “characters”), and its “deficit” sense, attested since the Taishō period, comes from marking negative sums in red ink.
Sanbutsu is from the Middle Chinese compound 產物, literally “produce + thing”.
Sū, “number”, is from Middle Chinese 數.
ストップ is borrowed from English stop.
タレント is a wasei eigo (pseudo-anglicism) derived from English talent.
Yurumeru is 緩 (yuru, “loose”) plus める (-meru, “-ify”).
Ōkata is the classical stem 大 (ofo) plus 方 (kata, “direction, way, side”).
Kyūshoku is ultimately from Middle Chinese 給食, literally “to give, to supply + food, meal”, sourced from the Records of the Grand Historian.
Juku is originally from Middle Chinese 塾 (MC dzyuwk).
In ishō, 装 is a daiyōji replacing 裳.
Nadakai is 名 (na, “name”) plus 高い (takai, “high, lofty”), with takai voiced to dakai by rendaku.
Atsukai is the continuative stem of the verb 扱う (atsukau, “to handle”).
Tsunami is 津 (tsu, “cove, inlet, outlet”) plus 波 (nami, “wave”), named so because tsunamis do more damage to sea ports.
Kōri is 小 (ko-, “little”) plus 売り (uri, “selling”).
ソロ is borrowed from Italian solo.
Hidarikiki is 左 (hidari, “left”) plus 利き (kiki, “effective”), with kiki voiced to giki by rendaku.
Someru is from Old Japanese 染む (somu), a lower bigrade verb.
